This is an editable scene captured from the real Gateway/Agent source-planning evaluation at `/tmp/autonomics-canvas-live-dNDUtr`. It contains no raster assets or credentials. The workflow passed its structural, actual-source retrieval, candidate review/adoption and export checks; those checks do not independently validate every scientific sentence.

Two statements in `note_scope_body` are intentionally retained as review defects: an unqualified database-wide absence claim, and an unsupported claim about Ser727 phosphorylation after nuclear entry. The opt-in `test:canvas:source-review:live` case asks the actual Agent to apply two explicit reviewer replacements through candidate feedback while preserving the rest of the graph, references and historical planning snapshot. It is a local feedback benchmark, not a scientifically approved example or an autonomous literature-review benchmark.

Primary records used for the review: [STAT1 Y701 phosphorylation](https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-873922), [STAT1 dimer release](https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-873927), and [STAT1 Ser727 phosphorylation](https://reactome.org/content/detail/R-HSA-909552). The actual retrieved record snapshots are retained with the original evaluation artifacts.

`scientific-ifng-reviewed.json` is the portable result of the explicit two-sentence caption review (`/tmp/autonomics-canvas-live-Xu6RXl`). The previous historical planning snapshot remains immutable; this fixture does not claim a full independent scientific audit.

`scientific-ifng-art-before-clearance.json` captures the actual model-selected generic receptor artwork and its fit before the failed note-movement workaround (`/tmp/autonomics-canvas-live-Vmot2Y`). Its label overlaps the original note region on purpose. The native `test:canvas:translate-notes` regression moves the existing note IDs instead of duplicating and deleting them. The SVG is “receptor” by Jan-Jezierski, distributed as CC0 in the BioIcons catalog: [source SVG](https://bioicons.com/icons/cc-0/Cell_membrane/Jan-Jezierski/receptor.svg), [CC0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/). Its original author, license, source URL and source/normalized hashes remain in the image metadata. The artwork is a generic illustration, not an IFNGR-specific molecular structure.
